gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independently measured figure for any of its three picks: The Gadgeteer measured the Beryl AX at about 300 Mbps WireGuard and 116 Mbps OpenVPN, NASCompares and Mighty Gadget each measured the Slate 7 at about 540 Mbps WireGuard and about 100 Mbps OpenVPN, and NASCompares measured the Beryl 7 drawing only 3.7–6.7 W and reaching a public Wi-Fi captive portal in about 35 s.
standout_why: I read stayingconnectedabroad.com (updated 2026-10-12), racksandwatts.com (2026-10-23) and itechguides.com (2026-08-11). Each one gives only GL.iNet's maximum figures and says it ran no measurements of its own. itechguides states that its picks are 'not independent head-to-head testing'. None of the three has a named reviewer's VPN speed, power draw, temperature or captive-portal time. I could not reopen the cited GL.iNet product pages for the Beryl 7 and Slate 7 because they returned HTTP 429. The cited Beryl AX datasheet PDF came back as unreadable binary. These are maker pages, so they hold maker claims. All three ChatGPT answers carried the caveat 'VPN speeds are manufacturer maximums, not guaranteed', and nothing in the results backed it with a test. The RTINGS Slate 7 review (result 16, never cited) did not render its test body when fetched.
decides: The tests back the current ranking without changing it. The Beryl AX's 300 Mbps WireGuard figure held up in The Gadgeteer's testing, which supports it as the value pick. The Beryl 7 measured lowest on power (3.7–3.8 W streaming, 6.4–6.7 W worst case with a USB SSD). That makes it the best fit for running from a power bank or a 15 W phone charger, which supports Best overall. The Slate 7 reached its WireGuard figure (about 540 Mbps, above GL.iNet's 490 Mbps listing) but measured about 100 Mbps on OpenVPN in both reviews, against the 385 Mbps on our page. It also drew more power (6–7 W idle, 8.1–8.2 W peak). Slate 7 buyers should use WireGuard, and the page should not present the 385 Mbps OpenVPN figure as tested.

findings.label: WireGuard throughput, measured (The Gadgeteer, Joe Porletto)
findings.source_title: GL-iNET Beryl AX GL-MT3000 Travel Router review - Stay cyber safe with this powerful device! - The Gadgeteer
findings.note: Published 2023-02-14, updated 2023-02-16. The reviewer ran 'a few speed tests' over about a month using the router as a network within the home network. VPN provider, line speed and client device are not stated. This matches GL.iNet's 300 Mbps WireGuard maximum.

findings.source_title: GL-iNET Beryl AX GL-MT3000 Travel Router review - Stay cyber safe with this powerful device! - The Gadgeteer
findings.note: Same test setup as the WireGuard figure. GL.iNet's maximum is 150 Mbps, so the measured result is 77% of it (116/150).

findings.label: Power draw, measured (CNX Software, Jean-Luc Aufranc)
findings.value: 3.5 W idle; 8.0 W during Wi-Fi 6 iperf3
findings.source_title: GL.iNet Beryl AX OpenWrt router review - WiFi 6 performance, repeater, NAS, and 4G hotspot modes - CNX Software
findings.note: Posted 2023-01-29, page header shows a 2024-01-14 update. Measured with LAN connected and Wi-Fi radios on; meter not named. The fan was off during the 8.0 W load reading.

findings.label: 5 GHz Wi-Fi iperf3 throughput, measured (CNX Software)
findings.source_title: GL.iNet Beryl AX OpenWrt router review - WiFi 6 performance, repeater, NAS, and 4G hotspot modes - CNX Software
findings.note: 60-second iperf3 runs with a Rock 5B SBC as the client; distance not stated. The first download run averaged only about 342 Mbps with 5,004 retransmissions, and the repeat run gave 911 Mbps with 0 retransmissions. No VPN was tested in this review.

findings.label: Power draw, measured (NASCompares, Rob Andrews)

findings.source_title: Gl.iNet Beryl 7 Review – Best Budget WiFi 7 Travel Router (NASCompares)
findings.note: Published 2026-02-13. Mixed load means several Wi-Fi clients, wired WAN and LAN both active, and repeated speed tests. Firmware not stated.

findings.label: Time to reach a public Wi-Fi captive portal, measured (NASCompares)
findings.source_title: Gl.iNet Beryl 7 Review – Best Budget WiFi 7 Travel Router (NASCompares)
findings.note: Timed from connecting to public Wi-Fi until the captive portal appeared. The same review measured cold boot to full interface at about 51 s and WAN failover between wired, repeater and tethered at about 4–5 s.

findings.label: VPN throughput, measured (NASCompares)
findings.value: OpenVPN DCO close to 1,000 Mbps over Ethernet; WireGuard 'approached' 1,100 Mbps
findings.source_title: Gl.iNet Beryl 7 Review – Best Budget WiFi 7 Travel Router (NASCompares)

findings.label: Case temperature, measured (NASCompares)
findings.value: 41–42 °C after 1 h of Wi-Fi streaming; 51–54 °C surface (vent about 56 °C) under heavier wired plus wireless load
findings.source_title: Gl.iNet Beryl 7 Review – Best Budget WiFi 7 Travel Router (NASCompares)

findings.note: Published 2025-03-05. Test conditions not stated. The review's spec table shows the same 540/100 Mbps figures, so the measured numbers may simply repeat that table. Our page lists GL.iNet's 490 Mbps WireGuard and 385 Mbps OpenVPN.

findings.label: Power draw, measured (NASCompares)
findings.note: Peak was at full load with multiple active connections. The same reviewer measured the Beryl 7 at 3.7–3.8 W while streaming.

findings.label: 5 GHz Wi-Fi throughput, measured (NASCompares)
findings.note: Client was a Wi-Fi 7 USB adapter; distance not stated.

findings.label: VPN throughput and power, measured (Mighty Gadget)
findings.value: WireGuard about 540 Mbps; OpenVPN about 100 Mbps; 7–8 W typical operation
findings.source_title: GL.iNet Slate 7 Review – Dual-band Wi-Fi 7 Travel Router with built-in AdGuard Home, Tailscale & VPN support (Mighty Gadget)
findings.note: Published 2026-01-09, updated 2026-03-20. VPN provider and server not stated. The reviewer also measured 5 GHz Wi-Fi at about 1,200 Mbps close to the router and 800–1,000 Mbps at typical distances, and 2.4 GHz at about 300 Mbps peak (150–200 Mbps at moderate distance). The OpenVPN result is about a quarter of the 385 Mbps on the Amazon listing (100/385 = 26%).

unsourced: RTINGS lab results for the Slate 7 (review page dated 2026-01-27) and the Beryl AX: both pages returned only navigation and no test results when fetched, so I took no RTINGS figures.
An RTINGS review of the Beryl 7 (GL-MT3600BE): a search found none.
An exact measured WireGuard Mbps figure for the Beryl 7: NASCompares only says it 'approached' 1,100 Mbps, and I found no other named reviewer with a number.
Named-reviewer measurements for the GL.iNet Opal (GL-SFT1200), TP-Link Roam 7 (TL-WR3602BE) and ASUS RT-AX57 Go: not searched because the 25-call budget was spent on the three ChatGPT picks.
Test conditions (VPN provider, server, firmware version) for the NASCompares, Mighty Gadget and Gadgeteer VPN results: none of the three articles states them.

The current maker VPN and power specs on the cited GL.iNet Beryl 7 and Slate 7 pages: both returned HTTP 429 on every try. The cited Beryl AX datasheet and the Beryl 7 datasheet PDFs came back as unreadable binary.

Beryl AX WireGuard figures from privacygear.pages.dev, dcspeedtest.com, thetestedhub.com and wirsingsecurity.com: they appeared only in search results, I did not open them, and the snippets contradict each other (265 to 900 Mbps), so they are left out.
